name: Spherical Dimension of Singletons
proof: For $n\geq3$, write $p_i$ and $m_i$ for the positive and negative literal at coordinate $i$. A partial labeling and its label flip are both realizable by singleton concepts exactly when they contain at most one literal of each sign. Thus the antipodal complex is the bipartite graph with edges $p_i m_j$ for $i\ne j$. The cycle $p_1,m_2,p_3,m_1,p_2,m_3,p_1$ is invariant under label flip, which acts as a half-turn, so it gives an equivariant copy of $S^1$. For the upper bound, choose distinct unit vectors $v_i$ in an open semicircle and send $p_i$ to $v_i$ and $m_i$ to $-v_i$. Extend linearly on each edge and normalize: the interpolated vector never vanishes, since the endpoints of an edge are not antipodal. This gives an equivariant map to $S^1$. An equivariant map from any $S^d$ with $d\ge2$ into the complex would therefore contradict Borsuk--Ulam. Hence $\mathrm{sd}=1$.
